## Summary

Define CFEL

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p{:occurrence}: [value format]{:value count};

p.*[name format]{:immediate name count};

p.**[name format]{:recursive name count};

p.*[name format]{:immediate name count}: [value format]{:value count}
```

### Prose Claim

CFEL (CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language) is the formal notation for
Subject addresses and fenced Formal Claims. CFEL is a model component beside
Graph and Carrier: Graph contains Nodes and Relations; CFEL addresses and
constrains them. CFEL syntax neither creates a Node, Relation, Property,
Carrier fact, Workflow step, nor evaluator result.

An `IF` membership condition can bind an unbound variable to each matching member of its declared selection; a variable already bound in the surrounding scope is tested against membership without rebinding. A parenthesized multi-line `THEN` body uses the same binding in each complete expression. This does not introduce a `FOR` primitive.

In a Formal Claim, `#model` and `#instances` are ordering comments for the model and instance expressions that follow; they do not assert graph facts. A `$variable` explicitly binds an anonymous selected Entity or instance; repeated occurrences in its scope select the same identity. A typed selector supplies its universe; use model variables where model entities are intended. These bindings introduce no new binding operator.

CFEL uses these graph-address forms:

- `X/Y` selects a narrower Primary Node; `X//Name` selects an existing
  instance of a declared kind, including a Property instance borne by its data bearer.
- `X.p` addresses Property p borne by X. A Subject selection may appear in an address or inside a filtered Node
  expression in a Formal Claim: `X/(.p := V)` combines an admitted Property
  value with selection of X. `:=` belongs to this Subject-selection syntax; it
  is not a free-standing Formal-Claim value assignment.
- `Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are opposite written views of one
  containment fact. `X >| Axis` and `Axis |< X` are opposite written views
  of one classification fact. A bare qualified address references its declared entity or instance. No `@` reference operator is required; `@N` identity/version tags retain their separate meaning.
- Parentheses group one expression. `;` separates complete expressions;
  a line break has no conjunction or disjunction meaning.

Text values use double quotes when needed to distinguish literal text from CFEL syntax; otherwise an unambiguous value may remain bare, including a multiword value such as `Scope Contract`. For example, `"A/B"` is text containing a slash. A name or path used as a reference retains its declared identity; a text value does not become a model reference. Within double-quoted text, `\"` represents a literal double quote and `\\` represents a literal backslash. Reject every other escape and any incomplete trailing backslash; JSON escape rules are not imported. This applies to values in Formal Claims and Subject selectors.

In Formal Claims, `X: Y` admits Y as an allowed value of X regardless of X's
kind or preceding path; it is not assignment. `=` and `!=` test conditions,
and `==` states a required or derived conclusion. `in` and `not in` are the
admitted membership tests. Numeric comparison and addition use the separately
defined `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` and `+`; they are distinct from Relation
operators. Property occurrence, direct-value, immediate-name
and recursive-name counts are distinct:

`{:n}`, `{:n+}` and `{:n..m}` state allowed cardinality bounds on their
qualified selection; `{=n}` tests a count condition, `{>n}` tests whether the
actual count is greater than n using the existing numeric `>`, and `{==n}`
concludes a required or derived count. These test/conclusion forms are not
allowed bounds. A Relation has independent outgoing and
reverse cardinalities: `Source {:forward}((RELATION)){:reverse} Target`.
A named Property has at most one occurrence per corresponding bearer; its applicable value constraints determine whether it is required. A present Property has a value, including nonempty child structure for a structural parent. `p: {:0..1}` specifies a direct-value count with its applicable inherited format. Other omitted annotations are unspecified, not zero. `[format]` applies to direct
values; a name selector is not a value selector. A `p.**` count aggregates
selected distinct descendant Property identities below p within each selected
bearer, independently of direct values and other bearers.

The named constructs `IF`/`THEN`, `UNIQUE`, `DETERMINES`, `COUNT`, `MAX`,
and `FENCED_LABELS` are admitted with the semantics in their own CFEL Rules.
`LOOKUP(R, q)` and `?==` are admitted CFEL operators with their own operator
Declarations; the `?==` ordered-assignment Rule supplies its chain semantics.
Boolean `AND` and `OR` combine conditions; parenthesize mixed AND/OR
expressions to state their grouping explicitly. `>>` is delivery notation with the
semantics of the delivery Rule; `!(selectors)` excludes branches from a
delivery selection. `Kind//$x` binds an existing selected instance and `$x.p`
reads its Property. Each non-graph CFEL operator has its own Declaration;
an operator is not a binary Node Relation. A Requirement/Declaration describes
a canonical or derived Relation direction; it does not authorize a second
stored inverse fact.

The reusable metadata family `Operator//Name == "notation literal"` binds a
declared operator descriptor to its token or bounded construct spelling. Its
quoted right side is metadata, not an executed CFEL expression, value assignment,
state creation, or a new model entity.

A direct Relation Declaration owns shared meaning and endpoints. A derived inverse Declaration retains the reverse HAS_INVERSE binding and its own alias, when present. A qualified or other non-inverse derived view retains its source, endpoint transformation and qualification; derivation alone does not imply unconditional endpoint reversal. `alias(Relation//NAME) == "token"` binds exact Relation names to lexical notation. `Relation//DIRECT <--> Relation//DERIVED` binds distinct inverse Relations in the direct Declaration. It never equates their identities. These metadata forms do not create literal-to-Node graph links.

A graph Relation connects declared model entities or declared instances,
including Carrier and CFEL; it is not limited to `Node/**`. A literal remains a
Property or allowed value, not a graph endpoint. A non-graph CFEL operator is
not itself a graph Relation, but its declared operator descriptor is a model
entity that may be a graph endpoint; an operator glyph or literal operand does
not create another model entity. Each direct Relation Declaration supplies shared meaning and a
formal Host/Target signature with typed selectors whose universe is known, or
with declared variables bound to that universe. Within a Relation Declaration
Formal Claim only, `$host ((RELATION)) $target` is the reusable generic
signature: its untyped variables range over that declared entity-or-instance
universe and exclude literals. It declares neither a Relation fact nor instance
data. Known endpoint kinds remain typed selectors. This generic Relation signature binding applies within Relation Declarations; typed bindings can also select model entities where their universe is declared.

Concrete directional alternatives describe the same canonical Relation fact:
`Step ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Workflow` and
`Workflow <((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Step`. The bare forward form
`Step ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Workflow` remains valid. In reverse writing,
normalization swaps canonical Source/Target and the two written endpoint count
slots. This syntax does not grant an inverse Relation permission. The Relation Declaration states the Host, Target and applicable counterpart direction. `HAS_INVERSE` applies to inverse Relations; a qualified non-inverse derived view retains its source, transformation and qualification.

In RMED Claims, all formal content is a fenced block labelled `CFEL`. CFEL
body syntax and Markdown-fence-label parsing are separate concerns. This Definition
describes the admitted language contract; it does not claim a complete parser
or evaluator. An unimplemented construct remains an adoption and conformance
gap, not evidence that the construct has different semantics.

This Definition does not convert a Format, Bool value, or any other value
into an instance selected by `//`. Such an instance selection requires the
existing source binding that declares it. No value-format-to-instance rewrite
is implied by the CFEL overview.

`Relation//IS_DECLARED_BY` is the qualified derived view of a GOVERNS fact whose source is a Requirement/Form Declaration; it reverses that selected fact while retaining the qualification. It is not a general inverse of GOVERNS or a permission for every Relation.

## Summary

Add basic CFEL queries with CTEs and SQL aliases

## Proposal

Extend CFEL with read-only queries. Use CFEL selectors in FROM, ordinary query names, reusable selection functions, and two result views: TABLE and FULL.

The Operator's latest example is the main query shape:

```CFEL
SELECT id, status, content
FROM atom//
WHERE atom in expand(CA-P-123, CONTAINS)
VIEW FULL;
```

SELECT chooses the Properties. FROM chooses the instances. WHERE filters them. VIEW controls how the selected data is shown.

## Sources and context

The query context supplies one Project snapshot and the selected source scope. CAPRMEDIO_MODEL and CAPRMEDIO_STRUCTURE name the two logical contexts: declared model and actual Project structure. They do not have to occupy FROM. This replaces the earlier suggestion that FROM could contain only those two names. No extra context keyword is proposed here.

FROM accepts a CFEL instance selector such as `atom//`, or a CTE name. `atom//` selects Current Atom instances and their narrower kinds. Current includes Done and Canceled where applicable; it is not the same as Status = Active. History queries remain separate.

A short selector is resolved against the model catalog in the supplied context. Ambiguous or unresolved names are errors. Sources are logical selections, not filenames, folders, database tables or physical columns.

## Names and optional aliases

With one source, bare Property names refer to its current item: `id`, `status`, `content.summary`. `atom` is the implicit item name for `FROM atom//`. It names the selected instance in this query, not the Atom kind or its Property declaration.

An explicit alias is optional:

```CFEL
SELECT atom.id, atom.content.summary AS summary
FROM atom// AS atom
WHERE atom.status = Active
VIEW TABLE;
```

An explicit AS alias replaces the implicit source name. Bare Property references remain available. Query aliases are ordinary names without `$`; existing `$` bindings in Formal Claims keep their meaning. A CTE can be read through bare output names or an explicit alias.

The examples propose these readable query aliases for existing model names:

| Query name | Model name |
| --- | --- |
| atom | Atom |
| id | ID |
| role | Role |
| form | Form |
| status | Status |
| content | Content |
| summary | Summary |

These aliases do not rename the model or its Carrier keys. This is an explicit alias set, not a general case-folding or underscore-conversion rule. Other names use their declared spelling or an admitted alias. Data values and Relation names keep their declared spelling.

## Views

SELECT controls the data in both views. Changing VIEW does not change which instances match or which Properties were selected.

| View | Output |
| --- | --- |
| TABLE | One row per result, with the selected expressions as columns. |
| FULL | One Atom block per result, with the selected Properties and Markdown content sections. |

The same selection can use either view:

```CFEL
SELECT id, status, content
FROM atom//
WHERE atom in expand(CA-P-123, CONTAINS)
VIEW TABLE;
```

Change only the last clause to `VIEW FULL;` to render Atom blocks. Do not add another Property list to VIEW.

Selecting `content` includes the complete Markdown content subtree. Selecting `content.claim` includes just that section. A Property container is projected as its nested Properties; this does not give the container a direct scalar value. TABLE keeps such a value in one column rather than expanding it into extra rows. FULL keeps the Atom's content structure and shows only the selected material; it is a result view, not a new authoritative Atom Carrier.

FULL needs one unambiguous source Atom per result. Plain Atom Property projections and AS labels retain that source identity through CTEs. A derived row without a unique Atom reference cannot use FULL. If DISTINCT combines results from different Atoms, FULL must report that ambiguity rather than choose an Atom. TABLE remains usable for those rows.

VIEW belongs to the final query. CTEs produce logical results, not rendered tables or Atom text. If VIEW is omitted, the caller receives the logical result without this proposal prescribing a presentation.

## Global selection functions

Define reusable functions in the CFEL query vocabulary, rather than copying a traversal into every query. They operate on the current query context; they do not register a stored Selection or change source objects.

Start with:

```CFEL
expand(CA-P-123, CONTAINS)
```

This returns the seed Atom and every instance reachable by following CONTAINS repeatedly, at all depths.

- Resolve the seed ID in the selected Current Project snapshot. A missing or ambiguous seed is an error.
- Include the seed.
- Follow only the selected Relation, in its stated direction, including a legitimately derived counterpart such as CONTAINS.
- Return each logical instance once, even when several paths reach it. Do not revisit a seen instance, so cycles terminate.
- Use the same snapshot for the seed, edges and returned instances.
- Return existing instance references. The function creates no Nodes, Relations, lifecycle changes or stored inverse links.

The second argument accepts one Relation name or a parenthesized, comma-separated list: `expand(seed, (relation1, relation2))`. Here the names stand for registered Relations. Treat the list as a set of permitted edge types; each hop may follow any member. An empty list is an error. A bounded-depth argument remains deferred.

The result can be used in identity membership:

```CFEL
WHERE atom in expand(CA-P-123, CONTAINS)
```

This is a function, rather than a simple alias, because it takes a seed and Relation as parameters. It is a proposed global selection function, not arbitrary user code or a storage-specific function.

## CTEs from the start

Include non-recursive WITH queries in the first version. A query can have several CTEs, separated by commas; each can read earlier CTEs in the same block.

```CFEL
WITH EpicTree AS (
  SELECT id, status, content
  FROM atom//
  WHERE atom in expand(CA-P-123, CONTAINS)
),
ActiveAtoms AS (
  SELECT id, status, content
  FROM EpicTree
  WHERE status = Active
)
SELECT id, status, content
FROM ActiveAtoms
ORDER BY id
LIMIT 20
VIEW FULL;
```

CTE names must be unique within the WITH block. Self-reference, forward references and cycles between CTEs are errors in this first version. Each body uses the same SELECT structure, without a nested WITH or a trailing semicolon. The final query ends with a semicolon.

A CTE returns named values or instance references. Source aliases and output fields have query-local scope and do not declare model entities. Plain Property projections preserve their source Atom identity; arbitrary computed rows do not acquire an Atom identity merely by having an ID column. Source or output aliases cannot be query keywords. Output column names must be unique.

Recursive graph selection through expand is included; recursive CTE evaluation remains deferred. These are different operations.

Do not require a particular materialization or number of executions. All reads and reused results must have the same logical meaning and errors within the selected snapshot. PostgreSQL and ClickHouse make different planning choices; their behavior is a reference, not an execution requirement for CFEL.

## First query structure

```text
[WITH name AS (query), ...]
SELECT [DISTINCT] expression [AS column], ...
FROM selector_or_cte [AS alias]
[WHERE condition]
[(SORT | ORDER BY) expression [ASC | DESC], ...]
[LIMIT number]
[VIEW TABLE | VIEW FULL];
```

This is an outline: brackets show optional parts and bars show alternatives. They do not introduce CFEL Format brackets or operators.

The logical order is FROM, WHERE, SELECT, DISTINCT, SORT, LIMIT, VIEW. WHERE reads source Properties and aliases, not SELECT aliases. SELECT expressions are evaluated for every surviving row before DISTINCT or LIMIT removes a row. Guarded conditions retain left-to-right CFEL short-circuiting.

SORT can read output names and source bindings. After DISTINCT it can read only output names, so it cannot choose an arbitrary source from a merged row. ASC is the default. Numeric and datetime order reuse the declared Format. Exact Unicode code-point text order is a new query proposal; it does not extend the existing MAX function. Without ordering, result order is unspecified. Use a unique final sort key when a repeatable limited subset matters.

## CFEL meanings and SQL aliases

Keep the existing meanings of `/`, `//`, `.`, `=`, `==`, `:`, `:=`, Relation expressions, guarded reads, identity membership and absence. The query aliases and functions are additions to the query context, not changes to existing Formal Claims.

| Query spelling | SQL alias | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SORT | ORDER BY | Order the same result. |
| != | <> | The same inequality test. |
| in / not in | IN / NOT IN | Existing instance-identity membership. |

Keywords may use either case. Value spelling does not change with keyword case.

An evaluated missing, invalid or unresolved value remains an error; it is not false. Omission is distinct from authored null, empty text, false and zero. Optional reads need an admitted guard or fallback. Collections remain collections: projection does not expand them into rows and scalar comparisons do not broadcast over them.

DISTINCT compares corresponding selected values using their Format's equality, and instance references by identity. An undefined equality rule is an error. It does not silently discard the Atom-identity ambiguity relevant to FULL.

COUNT of direct Property values and scalar MAX keep their existing CFEL meanings. The first version does not add SQL row COUNT, SELECT *, COUNT(*), or scalar-list IN. `*` and `**` retain their existing Property meanings. New row projection, global selection functions, CTEs and views need their own accepted query contract.

An empty result is valid. Unknown selectors, fields, aliases, CTEs or functions are errors, not a successful empty result.

## Starting references

| Reference | Starting point |
| --- | --- |
| [Dataview query structure](https://blacksmithgu.github.io/obsidian-dataview/queries/structure/) and [query types](https://blacksmithgu.github.io/obsidian-dataview/queries/query-types/) | Logical fields, readable filters, selected columns, sorting, limits and presentation. |
| [JQL clauses](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-service-management-cloud/docs/what-is-advanced-search-in-jira-cloud/), [keywords](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-service-management-cloud/docs/jql-keywords/) and [operators](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-service-management-cloud/docs/jql-operators/) | Readable field/operator/value conditions and Boolean composition. |
| [PostgreSQL SELECT](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-select.html) and [WITH](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/queries-with.html) | Query clauses, aliases and chained non-recursive CTEs. |
| [ClickHouse SELECT](https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select) and [WITH](https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select/with) | Similar query clauses with different storage and CTE execution choices. |

Use these as references, not full compatibility targets. Do not import their missing-value, coercion or storage rules into CFEL.

## Adoption work

1. Review this query shape, aliases, FULL/TABLE views and expand semantics.
2. Define the accepted query components and reusable functions in Core CFEL RMED.
3. Add examples for bare Properties, optional aliases, Current versus Active, guarded reads, nested content, both views, containment expansion, duplicate paths, cycles, chained CTEs, invalid inputs and empty results.
4. Implement the accepted contract in separate Engine work. Keep file, database, CLI and MCP connectors outside the logical language contract.

Defer joins, recursive CTEs, arbitrary subqueries, GROUP BY, HAVING, window functions, scalar-list IN, SQL row aggregates, full-text search, user-defined function bodies, writes and materialization controls. A registered selection helper such as expand is included; this does not open arbitrary function execution.

This is an Active Specification Proposal. It does not adopt the language changes or claim parser, evaluator or runtime support.

## Summary

Assign a default when an Object Property is absent

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p ?== expression
```

### Prose Claim



- `p ?== e1 ?== e2` is one ordered conditional-assignment chain. Keep p when it has an authored value; when p is absent, use the first available valid expression from left to right and set that missing Object Property value in the Model. An authored invalid value is an error, not absence. Omission is Property absence, not null, an empty string, zero or false.

- Expressions may be literals, same-bearer Property paths, explicit bound Property reads, or `LOOKUP(R, q)`. An explicit foreign-bearer read must resolve one target in the declared evaluation context; zero or multiple targets are errors.

- `LOOKUP(R, q)` is an admitted fallback expression; its value and traversal semantics are defined by the Operator//Lookup Declaration.

- Evaluate fallback expressions lazily from left to right; stop at the first valid available value. Later branches are not evaluated. Missing final values, evaluated fallback-expression cycles, and more than one applicable fallback chain are errors. Independent Declaration constraints still apply.

- The conditional assignment sets the missing Object Property value in the Model and the result must satisfy p’s declared value Format and cardinality, including required effective cardinality. It does not itself write a Carrier, persist a file, or create an authored Carrier occurrence; Carrier I/O remains the responsibility of an adapter or Delivery rule. Property-declaration inheritance is unchanged; recursive instance-value lookup occurs only through explicit LOOKUP.
## Details

```CFEL
# model
Atom.Header.Label ?== Atom.Header.Form
```

## Summary

Declare CFEL operator LOOKUP(R, q)

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Operator//Lookup == "LOOKUP(R, q)"
```

### Prose Claim

`LOOKUP(R, q)` is an existing contextual value expression admitted in a `?==` fallback expression. Starting at the bearer of target Property `p`, follow one existing outgoing link of declared Relation `R` at each step, in R's declared direction. Exclude the starting bearer. Return the nearest authored value of `q` that is applicable to that bearer. Resolve `q` by full Property declaration identity and effective MODEL applicability; skip only an inapplicable Property or an absent authored occurrence. At a known end with no applicable authored value, return absence. Do not match by bare name or invent a Property slot.

A present invalid value, unresolved applicability or graph fact, multiple outgoing targets, or revisiting a bearer is an error. Follow only the Relation direction named by R.

## Semantics

`Operator//Lookup` identifies the declared CFEL value-expression operator. The traversal semantics above are its complete existing contract.

## Summary

CFEL numeric range constraint

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p: [0..100]{:value count}
```

### Prose Claim

Inside a square-bracket value Format annotation, `lower..upper` is a closed numeric interval: both endpoints are included. It constrains each direct Property value and does not state Property occurrence or value cardinality. This square-bracket value constraint is distinct from the existing curly-brace cardinality range `{:n..m}`.

## Summary

CFEL Format constraint intersection

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p: [int, 0..100]{:value count}
```

### Prose Claim

A comma inside one square-bracket value Format annotation combines constraints by intersection. Each direct value must satisfy every listed constraint. Thus `[int, 0..100]` admits integer values from 0 through 100 inclusive. An empty or incompatible intersection admits no values. Existing curly-brace occurrence and value-cardinality annotations keep their current meanings and remain independent.
